SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.XII, VIJAYAPURA AT VIJAYAPURA AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL TO GRANT THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.14,99,990/-
ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BEFORE THIS HON'BLE IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY AND ETC.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY Smt. Vimala W/O Sukhadev Bandagar vs Sunil And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180703852/

has been filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') by the claimant in MVC No.839/2015 for the death of deceased Digambar and MFA No.200963/2021 has been filed by the claimant in MVC No.906/2015 being aggrieved by the common judgment and award dated 02.01.2021 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member MACT XII,
Vijayapura (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2.

The brief facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals are that on 21.04.2015 at about 9:30 AM deceased Digambar was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-13/BK-0738 along with Janardhan (claimant in MVC No.906/2015) to Dangare Petrol pump located on Degaon-Mangalweda road near the land of one Pappu Sugar and Gouri Karale, at that time, a TATA Tempo bearing Reg.No.MH-12/RA-1222 came from NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR opposite side driven by its driver in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, Digambar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries and Janardhan sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.

It was pleaded that they spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, funeral, etc.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement in which the averments made in the petitions were denied.
Respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal inspite of service of notice and was placed ex-parte.
5. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The mother of the deceased was examined NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR as PW-2, the injured claimant was examined as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries and the death of Digambar.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant in MVC No.839/2015 is entitled to compensation of Rs.7,18,000/- and the claimant in MVC No.906/2015 is entitled to global compensation of Rs.50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle to pay compensation amount along with interest to the claimants.
Being aggrieved,

sentences.text: these appeals have been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the claimants has raised the following contention:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR Reg:Negligence:
(i) The accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Tempo bearing registration No.MH- 12/RA-1222 which came in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the deceased who was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-13/BK-0738.
He further contended that immediately after the accident, a complaint has been lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The police have registered the FIR and after thorough investigation, filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
To prove the case, the claimants in both the cases have been examined as PWs.1 and 2.
PW.1 is the eyewitness who is also proceeding as pillion rider on the said motorcycle.
He has categorically stated that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
To disprove the evidence of claimants, respondent No.2 has not examined any witness.
Except examining its official, they have not examined the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Tribunal NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR has rightly held that driver of the offending vehicle is negligent in causing the accident.
Reg: Quantum in MVC No.839/2015:
(i) Firstly, the claimant claims that the deceased was aged about 24 years and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing business.
But the Tribunal is not justified in taking the monthly income of the deceased as only Rs.6,000/-.
(ii) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.
LTD. vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the established income is to be added towards 'future prospects'.

sentences.text: The same may be considered.
Hence, he prays for allowing the appeal.
Reg.:Quantum in MVC No.906/2015:
(i) Firstly, due to the accident, the claimant has suffered injuries.
He has suffered fracture of tibia and he was inpatient for a period of 08 days.

The global NC:
2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side, hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
Reg: Negligence:
(i) The rider of the motorcycle was riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the offending vehicle, as a result, the accident has occurred.
The rider of the motorcycle also contributed to the accident.

sentences.text: Tribunal has erred in holding that driver of the Goods Tempo alone is negligent in causing the accident.
Therefore, he contended that the deceased, rider of the motorcycle was also negligent in causing the accident.
Reg.: Quantum in MVC No.839/2015 8.
Even though the claimant claims that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, the same is - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR not established by the claimant by producing documents.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-
notionally.
(i) Secondly, since the claimant has not established the income of the deceased, the Tribunal rightly held that the claimant is not entitled for compensation towards 'future prospects'.
(ii) Thirdly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.
Reg: Quantum in MVC No.906/2015
(i) The injuries suffered by the claimant are minor in nature.
He has not examined the doctor.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the injured claimant, the global compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and it does not require any enhancement.
- 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR Reg: Liability 9.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence.
As such, the insured has violated the policy condition.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.
The Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from paying the compensation.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
11.

It is the case of the claimants that on 21.04.2015 at about 9:30 AM, the deceased Digambar was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-13/BK- 0738 along with a pillion rider Janardhan (claimant in MVC No.906/2015) towards Dangare Petrol Pump on Hiraj Cross road on Smt. Vimala W/O Sukhadev Bandagar vs Sunil And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180703852/
6 Degaon-Mangalweda Road, at that time, a truck bearing registration No.MH-12/RA-1222 being driven - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motorcycle.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, Digambar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries and Janardhan sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
12. To prove the case, claimants have examined Sri.Janardhan as PW-1, wife of deceased Smt.Vimala as PW-2 and produced 14 documents.
Respondent No.2 has examined an officer of the Insurance Company as RW-1 and produced 04 documents.
In their evidence, they have categorically stated that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
The driver was driving the offending Tempo in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Immediately after the accident, they have lodged the complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The police after thorough investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
PW.1 who is an eyewitness has categorically stated that - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR the driver of the offending Tempo was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
To disprove the evidence of claimants, respondent No.2 has not examined driver of the offending Tempo.
They have examined the officer of Insurance Company as RW.1.
Even in the cross- examination of PWs.1 and 2 nothing worthwhile information is elicited.

By considering the evidence of PWs.1 and 2, FIR (Ex.P1), complaint (Ex.P2), Panchanama (Ex.P3) and charge sheet (Ex.P6), the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that accident has occurred due to negligence of driver of Tempo bearing Reg.No.MH-12/RA- 1222.
Reg: Quantum in MVC No.839/2015 13.
The claimant claims that deceased Digambar was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing business.
But she has not produced any document to prove the same.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR taken place in the year 2015, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m.
To the aforesaid income, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in PRANAY SETHI (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,200/-.

Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.5,600/- has to be taken as his contribution to the Smt. sentences.text: The deceased was aged about 24 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.12,09,600/-
(Rs.5,600*12*18) on account of 'loss of dependency'.

14. In addition, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate'
and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd. -V- Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram And Others [2018 ACJ 2782], claimant i.e., mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of filial consortium' .

16. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 12,09,600
Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of Filial consortium 40,000

The claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,79,600/- as against Rs.7,18,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
- 16 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR Reg: Quantum in MVC No.906/2015 18.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Tempo.
The claimant has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula and right contusion, right forearm and other injuries all over the body.
He has not examined the doctor.

Considering the medical records and injuries suffered by the claimant, we are of the opinion that the global compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is required to be enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
He was not having a valid and effective driving licence as on the date to drive the said vehicle.
The insured has violated the policy condition.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
The said judgment is not challenged by the - 17 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR owner of the offending vehicle.
The owner is served before the Tribunal as well as before this Court.
Hence, respondent No.1 is served and unrepresented.

20. In view of judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another, [(2018)3 SCC 208], respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

21. Accordingly, we pass the following order:
(i) The appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) The judgments of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

(iii) The claimant in MFA No.200898/2021 is entitled to compensation amount of Rs.12,79,600/- as against Rs.7,18,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
- 18 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6519-DB HC-KAR
(iv) The claimants in MFA No.200963/2021 is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

(v) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount along with interest at 6% in both the appeals within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-

awarded by the Tribunal.
Considering the medical records and injuries suffered by the claimant, we are of the opinion that the global compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is required to be enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
He was not having a valid and effective driving licence as on the date to drive the said vehicle.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
